scope: Source-backed reconstruction of the public Orion guidance, navigation, and control architecture, navigation sensor roles, manual-control interfaces, propulsion effectors, and selected Artemis II as-flown control demonstrations while explicitly separating system capability from unavailable raw sensor, navigation-filter, guidance-command, controller-input, and thruster-firing histories.

sources.title: Artemis II Reference Guide
claims_used: Orion guidance, navigation, control, and propulsion software operates across multiple mission phases.
The software supports manual and automated modes.
The software can handle commands from the ground and crew.
Orion uses redundant navigation sensors appropriate to different mission phases.
Star trackers support attitude determination.
Inertial measurement units measure body rotation rates and accelerations.
GPS supplies position and velocity updates in Earth-proximate mission phases.
Deep Space Network measurements support deep-space spacecraft location determination.
The optical navigation camera uses Earth and Moon imagery for range and bearing information.
Sun sensors determine Sun direction during emergency safe mode.

sources.title: Avionics and Software
claims_used: The GNC&P system is responsible for knowledge of spacecraft state and trajectory and controls propulsion to maintain the required attitude and path.
GNC&P flight software runs on vehicle management computers.
The software receives navigation-sensor and pilot-control inputs.
The software commands appropriate spacecraft effectors.
The software operates in manual and automated modes and accepts ground and crew commands.
The onboard navigation architecture includes IMUs, GPS, star trackers, optical navigation, Sun sensors, and barometric altimeters.
Deep Space Network tracking supports location determination outside GPS range.

sources.title: How to Fly NASA's Orion Spacecraft
claims_used: The rotational hand controller commands spacecraft attitude.
The translational hand controller commands translation.
Manual-controller commands are detected by Orion guidance, navigation, and control flight software.
The flight software determines which reaction-control-system thrusters to fire and when.
Orion has 24 reaction-control-system thrusters.

sources.title: Artemis II Flight Update: Apogee Raise Burn Complete, Crew Looks Ahead to Proximity Operations
claims_used: The approximately 70-minute proximity-operations demonstration would test manual maneuvering relative to the detached ICPS.
The crew would use translational and rotational hand controllers.
Small close-range maneuvers would use European Service Module reaction-control-system thrusters.
An automated departure burn would conclude the demonstration.
Docking-camera measurements during departure would support engineering knowledge for future rendezvous navigation.

sources.title: Artemis II Flight Update: Proximity Operations Complete, Perigee Raise Burn Up Next
claims_used: The proximity-operations demonstration was completed.
The activity lasted approximately 70 minutes.
The crew performed controlled approach and retreat maneuvers relative to the detached ICPS.
The demonstration used onboard navigation sensors and reaction-control thrusters.
Orion executed an automated departure burn after the manual demonstration.

sources.title: Artemis II Flight Day 4: Crew Completes Manual Piloting Demonstration
claims_used: Christina Koch and Jeremy Hansen took turns controlling Orion.
The demonstration began at 9:09 p.m. EDT.
The crew manually piloted Orion for 41 minutes.
The demonstration tested six-degree-of-freedom and three-degree-of-freedom thruster modes.

sources.title: Artemis II Flight Day 8: Crew Conducts Key Tests on Return to Earth
claims_used: A manual piloting demonstration was planned for approximately 10:55 p.m. EDT.
The planned activity included centering a designated target and guiding Orion to a tail-to-Sun attitude.
Flight controllers later elected to forgo the manual piloting demonstration.

related_measurement_context.reason: NASA reporting describes engineering measurements during the departure burn; Phase 2J.1 does not promote the docking camera to a closed-loop onboard navigation input without explicit evidence.

guardrails: Navigation sensor capability does not establish an as-flown sensor measurement history.
AROW public OEM state vectors are flight-derived trajectory products and are not Orion's onboard navigation-filter state history.
Deep Space Network orbit determination is ground-based navigation support and is not an onboard sensor measurement.
A crew hand-controller command is processed by GNC flight software and is not itself a published thruster-firing history.
Installed RCS architecture does not establish the exact as-flown thruster sequence.
Manual piloting demonstration completion does not disclose the complete control law.
The names six degrees of freedom and three degrees of freedom do not reconstruct the underlying control algorithm.
The planned Flight Day 8 manual demonstration was foregone and must not be represented as executed.
Trajectory-correction outcomes do not expose the public guidance-command history.
Public GNC architecture does not expose Orion flight-software source code.
Public sensor descriptions do not expose navigation covariance history.
Public operational reports do not expose the complete Flight Director GNC rationale tree.
The docking-camera engineering measurement context is not promoted to a primary closed-loop Artemis II onboard navigation input without explicit source evidence.
Phase 2J.1 does not infer which propulsion engine class executed OTC3, RTC1, RTC2, or RTC3.
